entries.text: No backend, no id registry: the whole project rides inside the URL fragment.

entries.title: Build every sibling's messages from one dictionary
entries.text: The pattern the contract recommends: assemble the dictionary before Gantt.create() runs, since the sibling factories close over their config too early for the service to exist yet.

entries.title: Diagnose a missing translation at runtime
entries.text: state.get().resolutionOrder shows exactly which tables a lookup will try, in order — the fastest way to tell "the key is missing everywhere" from "the key is in a table this local…

entries.title: Let a partial translation degrade to English key by key
entries.text: A table that only covers part of the UI is normal, not an error — missing keys fall through to the caller's own default rather than showing blank or throwing.

entries.title: Add a menu entry and translate the built-in context menu
entries.text: Contributed entries stack after the built-ins automatically — no need to replace items to add one action, and messages carries the translation independently of the contribution.

entries.title: Add a search box, a filter panel, and a zoom toolbar together
entries.text: Three opt-in groups turned on at once — a chart with enough tasks that a reader needs to narrow it, plus a toolbar for reorienting the viewport without a keyboard shortcut cheat s…

entries.title: Turn on multi-select, the accessible click-move alternative, and group dragging
entries.text: A chart where selecting several tasks at once to move or delete them together is a normal thing to want, with a WCAG 2.2 non-dragging alternative for readers who cannot perform a…

entries.title: A tighter budget for a chart you are holding to a higher frame rate
entries.text: Default budgetMs assumes 60fps. Profiling against a stricter target (a kiosk display locked to 120fps, say) means lowering it so "over budget" actually means something for that ta…

entries.title: Record a trace around a specific operation and download it
entries.text: Capture exactly the frames and instants around one suspect operation — a bulk load, a big scroll — rather than eyeballing the live overlay, then hand the JSON to a colleague or a…

entries.title: Wire the overlay into a debug toggle instead of always showing it
entries.text: Ship the plugin (and its service) in every build, but keep the visible box off unless a developer explicitly asks for it — the loop performs no per-frame work while both the overl…

entries.title: Add the dashboard with a toolbar button, not on load
entries.text: The usual shape for a real application: the plugin is always composed (its services are cheap and headless), but the panel only appears when a reader asks for it.

entries.title: Build a traffic-light health board
entries.text: healthSummary() is the whole aggregation step — a host just maps the result onto whatever chips or rows its sidebar uses, with the status text always shown alongside any color.

entries.title: Clone a project as a template for a new engagement
entries.text: duplicateProject deep-copies a project's whole task subtree and its internal links as one undo step, optionally shifting every date to a new start.

entries.title: Custom metrics and a custom widget body
entries.text: formulas covers a project-specific number the standard nine widgets cannot name; renderWidget replaces one widget's card body wholesale — here, the overdue list becomes a one-line…

entries.title: Group tasks into projects and let a reader narrow to one
entries.text: The everyday shape: bind existing task subtrees to project nodes at setup, then let a picker built on the interaction plugin's filter service call applyPortfolioFilter with whiche…

entries.title: A read-only resource-axis view for a capacity review meeting
entries.text: The resource view alone, grouped by team, with no assignment editor composed — a viewing surface a lead can scan without also being able to edit it.

entries.title: A resource-load band with a policy capacity line
entries.text: Show total demand against a fixed capacity ceiling rather than the built-in per-resource sum — useful when headcount for a phase has not been decided yet, or a known blackout peri…

entries.title: A staffing dashboard: pool, assignments and over-allocation together
entries.text: The everyday combination: a named roster, the column and editor to assign it, and both read-only over-allocation surfaces on by their own defaults.

entries.title: Run a CI-style structural check with no UI at all
entries.text: The diagnostics service works headless — fail a build on unlinked tasks or negative-lag leads without ever mounting the panel.

entries.title: Shade a working calendar and stop scheduling into holidays
entries.text: The everyday calendars shape: one company calendar, its holidays visible on the chart, and automatic scheduling that already routes around them.

entries.title: Show reviewers the chain that actually drives the finish date
entries.text: No config beyond turning the nest on: classification, outlines and link emphasis are all default-on the moment criticalPath is present.

entries.title: Turn dependency links into a schedule that keeps itself consistent
entries.text: Links alone are just lines. Turning propagation on makes editing one task move everything the links say follows it, in a single undo step.

entries.title: Decorate the default bar instead of replacing it
entries.text: The usual mistake with renderBar is redrawing everything.

entries.title: Distinguish task types without relying on colour
entries.text: Required whenever fill colour carries meaning: a colour-blind reader, a greyscale print and a projector all lose hue before they lose texture or shape.

entries.title: Make short bars grabbable on a tablet
entries.text: A one-day task at month zoom is a two-pixel target.

entries.title: Classify tasks and show it without relying on color alone
entries.text: The badge's letter keeps RAG status readable in greyscale; the optional recolor is the fast, at-a-glance version for a status-focused view.

entries.title: Compare the live schedule against the plan of record
entries.text: The everyday baselines shape: capture the plan once, then let the underlay and slip triangles do the rest of the talking.

entries.title: Cost a project from assignments alone
entries.text: The minimum viable setup: seed rates for the resources already assigned in the data, and every task's labor cost computes itself.

entries.title: Read EVM budgets from cost instead of duplicating them
entries.text: Skip meta.evm.bac entirely and let evm fall back to cost's estimated cost per task, so a budget is entered once.

entries.title: Flag late work and explain the colors
entries.text: The everyday combination: turn on the overdue warning, add one custom rule for a status your team tracks, and let readers see what each color means instead of memorizing it.

entries.title: Localize headers, dates and Name sorting together
entries.text: The three pieces of a translated grid that have to move together: retitled headers, locale-formatted cells, and a Name column that sorts the way that locale expects.

entries.title: Read-only status board with a WBS column
entries.text: A chart meant for viewing, not editing — a reporting view or a shared dashboard — with the work-breakdown code visible and folded branches showing how much they hide.

entries.title: The standard status/priority/deadline board, with avatars
entries.text: The common case: enough columns to triage a schedule at a glance, status visible on the bars themselves, and ownership visible without opening a row.

entries.title: A single undo/redo chord, no macOS alternates, with silent announcements
entries.text: Replace the default chord list entirely for a chart embedded in a host that already owns Ctrl+Shift+Z for something else, and suppress the aria-live wording in favor of the host's…

entries.title: Carry undo history across a locale change
entries.text: locale is a create()-time option, so switching it means dispose and recreate.

entries.title: Drive a toolbar's disabled state from the history store
entries.text: No bindButtons() helper — subscribe to the store directly, which is one line and needs no extra API to learn.

entries.title: Build a right-to-left chart base
entries.text: Set the chart's reading direction once, so every plugin that consults ViewService.direction() can mirror consistently — remembering that today, only this plugin's own scrollbars a…

entries.title: Highlight a release freeze without touching the calendar
entries.text: A zone is the right tool when the span is a project fact, not a working-day fact — it needs no calendar data and no per-task field.

entries.title: Ship an in-app high-contrast toggle
entries.text: Give users an accessibility switch that swaps the whole palette at runtime, rather than shipping two builds or asking them to change their OS settings.

entries.title: Show a fiscal calendar to a Tokyo-based team
entries.text: Combines a fiscal year offset with wareki-era labels and a local display zone — three independently orthogonal timeline options that commonly travel together for this kind of audi…

entries.title: Show a status date alongside today, for a locked weekly report
entries.text: The chart may be opened any day, but the progress figures on it are only ever correct as of the last status date.

entries.title: Start a chart already in table view
entries.text: An embed whose first job is letting the reader scan and edit fields, not read a timeline — skip the chart entirely on first paint instead of asking the reader to switch to it.

entries.title: Tune the performance tier for very large datasets
entries.text: At ten-thousand-plus rows, moving per-frame cost off the scrolling frame and clipping repaints to what actually changed is the difference between a smooth fling and a visible stut…
